prompt.context: Premium Paints Ltd. (PPL) is a company that sells 'premium' paints for the interior and exterior of homes. PPL currently only sells paint in the UK. Premium (or 'posh') paints are priced at a premium to 'standard' paints, and market themselves as having better colour density and a better finish. The market for premium paints has grown substantially over the last two decades, led by PPL, which is the market leader in premium paint with sales of 4 million litres of paint in 2013. PPL has hired Parthenon-EY to answer three questions.
prompt.question:
Q1: What percentage of UK households does PPL serve with its paint products?
Q2: How large (in £) is the total premium paint market in the UK in 2013?
Q3: What percentage of total paint sales (£) were premium paint sales in 2013?

clarifying_info.q: What size tins does PPL sell paint in?
clarifying_info.a: PPL only sells paint in 5-litre tins.

clarifying_info.q: What is the average price per litre of premium vs. standard paint?
clarifying_info.a: The average price per litre of premium paint is £20; the average price per litre of standard paint is £10.

clarifying_info.q: How many rooms does a household paint per redecoration?
clarifying_info.a: On average, people paint 4 rooms per redecoration.

clarifying_info.q: How much paint is needed per room?
clarifying_info.a: On average, it takes 5 litres of paint per room.

clarifying_info.q: How many households are there in the UK?
clarifying_info.a: There are 25 million households in the UK.
On average, PPL customers paint once every 4 years (i.e., the redecoration cycle is 4 years).

exhibits.title: UK Paint Market – Market Share of Premium vs. Non-Premium Paints (Volume)
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing the split between premium paint brands and non-premium paint in the UK market by volume. Within the premium segment, PPL's share of the premium paints market is shown alongside a competitor (Fired Earth).

exhibits.title: Addressable Market – Current Penetration (Premium and Total Market Calculations) Diagram
exhibits.shows: A diagram showing the calculation chain from total UK households through to PPL-addressed households and paint spend figures, including intermediate values and assumptions used in the market sizing.

framework: Start with total UK households (25M) and use paint consumption data to estimate the total number of households that use premium paint

Determine PPL's customer base using PPL's known sales volume (4M litres), consumption per household (4 rooms × 5L = 20L per redecoration), and adjust for the 4-year redecoration cycle to get annual figures
Convert PPL households to a % of total UK households (Q1)
Scale from PPL's volume to total premium market volume using PPL's 50% market share, then convert to value using £20/L (Q2)
Calculate total paint market value (premium + standard) by sizing the non-premium segment using remaining households, then compute premium as a % of total (Q3)

questions.prompt: Q1: What percentage of UK households does PPL serve?
questions.guidance: Candidate must build the chain: PPL sells 4M litres/year. Each household uses 4 rooms × 5L = 20L per redecoration. On a 4-year cycle, annual usage per household = 20L/4 = 5L/year. So PPL serves 4M ÷ 5 = 800K households per year. Over a 4-year cycle, total addressable households = 800K × 4 = 3.2M... but the question asks how many are 'addressed' (meaning when they do paint, they use PPL), so the key figure is 800K households/year out of 25M total = 3.2% of UK households. Strong candidates will identify the redecoration cycle assumption proactively.

math.setup: PPL litres/year ÷ (litres per household per redecoration ÷ redecoration cycle years) = PPL-addressed HHs per year
steps: Litres per household per redecoration = 4 rooms × 5L = 20L
Annual litres per PPL household = 20L ÷ 4 years = 5L/year
PPL households using PPL in any given year = 4,000,000L ÷ 5L = 800,000 HHs
math.answer: 800,000 households use PPL each year, representing 3.2% of all UK households

questions.prompt: Q2: How large (£) is the total premium paint market in the UK in 2013?
questions.guidance: Candidate must convert PPL's volume to total premium market volume using PPL's 50% market share (from Exhibit 1), then multiply by the £20/L premium price. PPL volume = 4M litres → total premium market = 4M ÷ 50% = 8M litres → value = 8M × £20 = £160M.

math.setup: PPL volume ÷ PPL market share = total premium volume; total premium volume × price per litre = total premium market value
steps: Total premium market volume = 4M litres ÷ 50% = 8M litres

questions.prompt: Q3: What percentage of total UK paint sales (£) were premium paint sales in 2013?
questions.guidance: Candidate must size the non-premium (standard) segment. Remaining UK HHs = 25M − 1.6M premium HHs = 23.4M HHs. (Note: 1.6M premium HHs = 8M litres total premium ÷ 5L/year per HH.) Each standard HH uses 20L per redecoration ÷ 4 years = 5L/year × £10 = £50/year. Standard market value = 23.4M × 5L × £10 = £1.17B. Total paint market = £160M + £1,170M = £1,330M. Premium share = £160M ÷ £1,330M ≈ 12%.

math.setup: Compute standard paint market value from remaining HHs, then premium % = premium value ÷ (premium value + standard value)
steps: Number of premium HHs = 8M litres ÷ (20L/redecoration ÷ 4 years) = 8M ÷ 5 = 1.6M HHs
math.answer: Premium paints represent approximately 12% of total UK paint sales by value

brainstorming.prompt: Do you think other markets would be attractive for international expansion? How would you go about assessing the most attractive opportunities?

categories.name: Market Size & Growth
ideas: Size of the overall paint market in the target country
Current penetration of premium paints vs. standard paints
Growth trajectory of the premium segment (momentum)
GDP per capita as a proxy for consumer willingness to pay a premium

categories.name: Competitive Landscape
ideas: Presence and strength of incumbent premium paint brands
Ease of entry and potential for PPL to differentiate
Barriers to entry (regulation, distribution, brand recognition)

categories.name: Consumer & Cultural Fit
ideas: Home ownership rates (renters less likely to invest in premium paint)
Attitudes toward home decoration and DIY culture
Frequency of redecoration in target market

categories.name: Operational Feasibility
ideas: Need for local manufacturing vs. exporting from UK
Regulatory requirements for paint products in the target market

categories.name: Prioritisation Approach
ideas: Score markets on premium segment size and growth rate first
Assess operational complexity and entry cost last
Start with markets culturally and economically similar to UK (e.g., Western Europe)

recommendation: PPL currently addresses only 3.2% of UK households and holds 50% of the premium segment, which itself is ~12% of the total UK paint market by value (£160M out of ~£1.33B)

The premium segment is small relative to the total market, suggesting significant headroom either in growing premium penetration in the UK or expanding internationally to replicate the model in larger or faster-growing markets
risks: Premium segment growth may slow as the UK market matures
International expansion introduces currency, regulatory, and operational complexity
Competitors like Fired Earth could erode PPL's 50% share if PPL focuses resources on expansion
next_steps: Analyse premium paint penetration trends in comparable European markets to identify highest-potential expansion targets
Assess whether PPL can grow UK premium penetration beyond the current 6.4% of HHs through marketing or channel expansion
Evaluate supply chain and manufacturing footprint required to support international growth
